findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is never true for spawn-context processes, so hung flushers are never killed
findings.body: Processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which yields `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess` but is NOT a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (= `multiprocessing.context.Process`), so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` evaluates to False in production. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally; the new guard means a process detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`) is never killed, yet a replacement process for the same shards is started immediately. The still-running old process and the new one then both flush and produce the same shards concurrently, leading to duplicate segments on buffered-segments and leaked processes/Redis+Kafka connections on each restart (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per index). The same false check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is also never called there. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or check `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

findings.title: join() stops iterating at the deadline and leaves remaining processes un-terminated
findings.body: In `join()`, once `remaining_time <= 0` the loop `break`s, so any processes later in `self.processes` never get `process.terminate()` called. Previously the single process was always terminated after the wait. With several flusher processes and a slow first process, subsequent processes are left running past join, continuing to flush against Redis while the consumer is rebalancing/shutting down. The deadline check should only skip the waiting, not the terminate call.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" vs "shard"
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `{"shards": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `{"shard": shard_tag}` (and `flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard` with a single int). This splits the same dimension across two tag keys, breaking dashboards/queries that group by `shard`. Also note `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list, so the value set differs from the per-shard int used by `flusher_unhealthy`.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is defined but never called anywhere in the module or tests. It also would create a second process for an index without killing/replacing the existing one. Remove it or wire it in.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) in test is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at the top, then calls `time.sleep(0.1)` with the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change". The call does nothing, so the test does not actually give the flusher thread any time; whether the segment is flushed before `step.join()` sets `stopped` is left to scheduling luck, making the test flaky rather than fixed. Use the original sleep (e.g. save a reference before patching) or poll until `messages` is non-empty.

findings.title: Docstring claims one process per shard but default is a single process
findings.body: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but the CLI option `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1 and `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))`, so by default all shards share one process exactly as before. Additionally, `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means passing `0` silently selects one-process-per-shard rather than being rejected. The docstring and help text should describe the actual behaviour (shards are distributed round-robin over at most N processes).

findings.title: Unrelated documentation change bundled into flusher PR
findings.body: The hasattr/isinstance guidance added to CLAUDE.md has no relation to the span-buffer flusher refactor described in the PR. Bundling unrelated changes makes review and revert harder; it should be split into its own PR.
